extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent attorneys/agents, and applicants involved in US patent prosecution
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing examiner-applicant interviews and the form/content requirements for amendments filed under 37 CFR 1.121 during U.S. patent prosecution (MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check applicant interview summary for accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s summary of what took place at the interview should be carefully checked to determine the accuracy of any argument or statement attributed to the examiner during the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an inaccuracy directly affects patentability, point it out in the next Office letter. If claims are allowable for other reasons, examiner should send a letter setting forth his/her version. If record is complete and accurate, place 'Interview record OK' on the paper recording the interview with date and examiner initials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark interview record OK when accurate
rubrics_metrics.description: If the record is complete and accurate, the examiner should place the indication 'Interview record OK' on the paper recording the substance of the interview along with the date and the examiner’s initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to confirm an agreed-upon record for IFW processing; see IFW Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on interviews after appeal brief or after application passed to issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in unusual situations, no interview is permitted after the brief on appeal is filed or after an application has been passed to issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews after those procedural events are exceptional and generally not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews appropriate before first reply in limited circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview may be appropriate before applicant’s first reply when the examiner has suggested that allowable subject matter is present or where it will assist applicant in judging the propriety of continuing the prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when helpful to clarify whether to continue prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office employees forbidden to communicate with unregistered/suspended/excluded representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Office employees are forbidden to hold oral or written communication with an unregistered or a suspended or excluded attorney or agent regarding an application unless that person is the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 105 for exceptions and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority required to participate in interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are generally not granted to persons who lack proper authority from the applicant or attorney/agent of record in the form of a paper on file in the application; a mere power to inspect is not sufficient authority for granting an interview involving the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesting party should have authority to bind the principal; absence of proper authority is grounds to deny interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered local representatives not of record generally denied interviews without POA
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are generally not granted to registered individuals who are the local representatives of the application unless a power of attorney to them is of record in the particular application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to 37 CFR 10.57(c) a practitioner cannot authorize other registered practitioners to conduct interviews without the client's consent after full disclosure; non-practitioners cannot be authorized to conduct interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone interview POA/facsimile recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: While a registered practitioner not of record may request a telephone interview if authorized by the applicant or the attorney of record, it is recommended that a facsimile transmission of a power of attorney be filed prior to the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If POA not filed, examiner may conduct the telephone interview with the Office’s file closed and work solely from the practitioner's file, which can be difficult over the phone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews normally require authority to bind the principal
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews normally should not be granted unless the requesting party has authority to bind the principal concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures the interview can lead to binding decisions or agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of telephone/e-mail/video conference for remote parties
rubrics_metrics.description: For remote practitioners, telephone, electronic mail, or video conference interviews may be valuable; Office policy places emphasis on telephone interviews initiated by the examiner to attorneys and agents of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner can often suggest minor changes by phone that result in allowance; major issues should be concisely stated and a further prearranged interview suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include examiner with negotiation authority when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: For an interview with an examiner who does not have negotiation authority, arrangements should include an examiner who does have such authority and who is familiar with the application so authoritative agreement may be reached at the time of the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents delays due to lack of authority to resolve substantive matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouped interviews for remote in-person attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: Grouped interview practice is effective for attorneys remote from the Washington, D.C. area who prefer personal or video conference interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prearranged interviews tied to prompt supplemental amendments can give the application special status and prompt special action.

rubrics_metrics.name: No discussion of inter partes questions ex parte
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may not discuss inter partes questions ex parte with any of the interested parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects procedural fairness and confidentiality of inter partes matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hide unrelated files prior to in-room interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to an interview in the examiner’s room, the examiner should arrange his or her desk so that all files, drawings and other papers, except those necessary in the interview, are placed out of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 101 for background; prevents exposure of other cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models/exhibits: admission to record only if comply with 37 CFR 1.91
rubrics_metrics.description: A model or exhibit may be exhibited or demonstrated during the interview, but a model or exhibit will not generally be admitted as part of the record unless it complies with 37 CFR 1.91; a model/exhibit submitted by applicant which complies with 1.91 would be made part of the application record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If used only for demonstration during the interview, it will not generally be made part of the record; a full description of what was demonstrated must be made of record per 37 CFR 1.133(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Large demonstrations outside the Office allowed with approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrations of apparatus or exhibits too large to be brought into the Office may be viewed by the examiner outside of the Office with the approval of the supervisory patent examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presumed necessary only when essential to develop or clarify issues involved in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: One interview normally permitted after final rejection with written purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, one interview after final rejection is permitted; prior to the interview, the intended purpose and content should be presented briefly, preferably in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interview may be granted if examiner is convinced disposal or clarification for appeal may be accomplished with only nominal further consideration. Interviews merely restating arguments or proposing new limitations requiring more than nominal reconsideration or new search should be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews during statutory periods after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews may be held after the expiration of the shortened statutory period and prior to the maximum permitted statutory period of 6 months without an extension of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 706.07(f) for statutory timing context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further interviews after final rejection only if they expedite appeal/disposal
rubrics_metrics.description: A second or further interview after a final rejection may be held if the examiner is convinced that it will expedite the issues for appeal or disposal of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner discretion; must materially advance resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after application sent to issue are generally not appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: After an application is sent to issue, an interview that would involve a detailed consideration of claims sought to be entered and discussion of prior art to determine allowability should not be given because the application is technically no longer under the primary examiner's jurisdiction (37 CFR 1.312).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments presented informally after issuance cannot be demanded as a matter of right; requests for interviews on cases where a notice of allowance has been mailed require Technology Center Director approval and a written showing of extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: All amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 (as revised)
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments filed on or after July 30, 2003 must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 as revised to facilitate electronic image processing; noncompliant amendments will receive a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP summarizes the revised practice and provides specific form/content requirements to facilitate electronic processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment document sectioning and order
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section of an amendment document (Specification Amendments, Claim Amendments, Drawing Amendments, and Remarks) must begin on a separate sheet to facilitate indexing and electronic scanning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended order: (A) cover sheet/table of contents with application info and page locations; (B) 'Amendments to the Specification' (separate sheet); (C) 'Amendments to the Claims' (separate sheet) including complete listing of all claims ever presented; (D) 'Amendments to the Drawings' (separate sheet) describing drawing changes; (E) remarks section (separate sheet); (F) any drawings including Replacement/New/Annotated sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendment methods and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the specification (other than claims, computer listings, sequence listings) must be made by adding, deleting or replacing a paragraph, by replacing a section, or by a substitute specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment must unambiguously identify the paragraph to be modified (paragraph number, page/line, or other unambiguous method) and be accompanied by replacement/new paragraphs. Replacement paragraphs must include markings showing changes; new paragraphs presented in clean form without underlining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking conventions for specification changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The full text of any replacement paragraph must be provided with markings to show all changes relative to the previous version. Added subject matter must be shown by underlining; deleted matter must be shown by strike-through except that double brackets may be used for deletion of five or fewer consecutive characters or when strike-through cannot be easily perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double brackets are square brackets [ ], not parentheses. If strike-through cannot be perceived, double brackets must be used; alternatively extra text may be included in strike-through then underlined with desired change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement sections and substitute specification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement sections must be submitted with markings to show all changes; substitute specifications require a clean version, a separate marked-up version showing changes, and a statement that the substitute contains no new matter per 37 CFR 1.125.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same marking rules (underline for additions, strike-through or double brackets for deletions) apply to replacement sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of previously deleted paragraphs/sections
rubrics_metrics.description: A previously deleted paragraph or section may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment adding the previously deleted paragraph or section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A direction by applicant to remove a previously entered amendment will not be permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims amendments must rewrite entire claim and include complete claim listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to a claim must be made by rewriting the entire claim with all changes (except when the claim is being canceled). Each amendment document that includes a change, cancellation, or addition must include a complete listing of all claims ever presented in the application; the claim listing replaces all prior versions of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the claim listing, the status of every claim must be indicated after its claim number using identifiers such as (Original), (Currently amended), (Canceled), (Withdrawn), (Previously presented), (New), and (Not entered).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim status identifiers and acceptable alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Status identifiers prescribed by 37 CFR 1.121(c) must be used (original, currently amended, canceled, withdrawn, previously presented, new, not entered); the Office will accept certain alternative status identifiers to prevent delays if the status is accurate and clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable alternatives are provided (e.g., 'Original Claim' for 'Original', 'Presently amended' for 'Currently amended', 'Canceled without prejudice' for 'Canceled', etc.). Examiners are not required to correct acceptable alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings for claim changes: strike-through/underlining/double brackets
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims being currently amended must be presented with markings to indicate changes relative to the immediate prior version: strike-through for deleted matter and underlining for added matter, with two exceptions—double brackets may be used for deletion of five or fewer consecutive characters and must be used when strike-through cannot be easily perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An accompanying clean version is not required and should not be presented. Only claims with status 'currently amended' or 'withdrawn' if being amended shall include markings. Added claims must be indicated as 'new' and their text must not be underlined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of claim text and clean versions
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of all pending claims not being currently amended shall be presented in the claim listing in clean version (no markings). Presenting a claim in clean version asserts it has not changed relative to the immediate prior version (except omission of markings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim being canceled must be indicated as 'canceled' and the text must not be presented. Canceled and not-entered claims must be listed only by claim number and status identifier (though Office may accept submitted text to avoid issuing a non-compliant amendment notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim cancellation and reinstatement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancellation of a claim is effected by an instruction to cancel a particular claim number and a canceled claim can be reinstated only by adding the claim as a 'new' claim with a new claim number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No renumbering of remaining claims—original numbering must be preserved throughout prosecution; when adding new claims, number them consecutively beginning with the number next following the highest numbered claim previously presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim numbering and ordering requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims in each amendment paper must be presented in ascending numerical order. Consecutive claims having the same status of 'canceled' or 'not entered' may be aggregated into one statement (e.g., Claims 1–5 (canceled)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example listings are provided in the MPEP to illustrate proper formatting and status labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing amendment requirements and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes to an application drawing must comply with 37 CFR 1.84 and must be submitted on a replacement sheet of drawings (or new sheet). Replacement sheets must be attachments to the amendment document and labeled in the top margin as 'Replacement Sheet'; new sheets labeled 'New Sheet'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement sheet must include all figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is amended. The figure/figure number must not be labeled 'amended'. All drawing changes must be explained in detail in the drawing amendment or remarks section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotated drawing sheets and when required
rubrics_metrics.description: A marked-up copy of any amended drawing figure (including annotations indicating changes) may be included and must be clearly labeled 'Annotated Sheet' and presented in the amendment or remarks section that explains the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A marked-up copy must be provided when required by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure consistency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures claims, specification, and drawings are in substantial harmony; Office may require such amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter in amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition—adding content not originally disclosed is not permitted; substitute specifications require a statement that no new matter is introduced as per 37 CFR 1.125.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for examiner’s amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification, including the claims, made by the Office in an examiner’s amendment may be made by specific instructions identifying precise insertion/deletion points, and compliance with certain paragraphs of 1.121 is not required for examiner’s amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's amendments have special procedural leeway compared to applicant-filed amendments.
